# 大丈夫論

**ID:** T1577
**Volume:** T30
**Category:** 中觀部類
**Original Category:** 中觀部
**Byline:** 提婆羅菩薩造  北涼 道泰譯
**Dynasty:** 北涼
**Date:** 397–439
**Juans:** 2
**CBETA:** https://cbetaonline.dila.edu.tw/zh/T1577

## Contributors
- 提婆羅 (A001209)
- 道泰 (A001526)

## Summary (Ask Bunkankun 聞分館君)

A two-fascicle Mahāyāna doctrinal-poetic treatise on the bodhisattva-mahāsattva ("great man" / *mahāpuruṣa*) ideal, organised around the perfection of giving (*dānapāramitā*). The text is structured as a sustained *kāvya*-style exposition of the figure of the bodhisattva, treating thirty doctrinal *pǐn* 品 ("examination of giving" 施勝品, "examination of the merit of giving" 施福品, etc.). Translated at the Northern Liáng 北涼 (397–439) court of the Héxī 河西 corridor (modern western Gansu) by the *śramaṇa* [道泰](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%81%93%E6%B3%B0) Dàotài 道泰, who was active in the Northern-Liáng translation programme c. 414–426 and is best known for his collaboration with [浮陀跋摩](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%B5%AE%E9%99%80%E8%B7%8B%E6%91%A9) Buddhavarman on the *Āpítán pípóshā lùn* 阿毘曇毘婆沙論 ([KR6l0011](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6l/KR6l0011), T1546).

**Abstract**

T1577 opens with a *maṅgala*-verse: "I bow respectfully to the perfectly enlightened, the great-compassion-grieving World-Honoured One, who through the perfection of giving has reached perfect awakening" 敬禮等正覺，大悲哀世尊… The body of the work is a sustained praise-and-exposition of the figure of the *mahāsattva* "great being" — translated into Chinese as 大丈夫 "great man" (a calque of *mahāpuruṣa*) — whose distinguishing characteristic is unstinting generosity. The work develops a doctrine of *dāna* in which the perfections of giving accumulate progressively, each chapter introducing a higher form of generosity (gift of material goods → gift of body → gift of life → gift of self).

The Indic original is no longer preserved in Sanskrit, and there is no known Tibetan parallel; T1577 is the unique witness to this particular Mahāyāna *dānapāramitā* treatise. The work has affinities with the *Bodhisattvabhūmi* of the Yogācāra Yogācārabhūmi, the *Suvarṇaprabhāsottama-sūtra*'s "Vyāghraparivarta", and the *Jātaka*-narrative tradition of the bodhisattva's exemplary self-sacrifice. The Northern-Liáng translation context — a Héxī corridor monastery operating at the cultural junction of India, Central Asia, and Han China — accounts for the work's preservation in Chinese alone.

The author named in the colophon as 提婆羅菩薩 (\*Devala) is distinct from [提婆菩薩](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%8F%90%E5%A9%86%E8%8F%A9%E8%96%A9) Āryadeva; the additional syllable 羅 is preserved in all canon-witnesses and is unlikely to be a scribal error.
